title: Product Status Label
prompt: A C# catalog endpoint shows a simple status label. Write a function that returns "Active" when isActive is true and "Inactive" when it is false.

explanation.beginner:
Example: productStatusLabel(true) produces "Active". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “labels inactive values”: input [false] produces "Inactive". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “labels inactive values”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
